content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The bookmark manager specification is ready for review:

- Feature directory: [`specs/001-bookmark-manager`](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager)
- Specification: [spec.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- Quality checklist: [requirements.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)
- Validation: all 16 checklist items pass; no unresolved clarifications.

The draft covers private bookmark libraries, tags, search/filtering, editing, deletion, duplicate detection, edge cases, and measurable outcomes. Sharing, folders, browser extensions, and bulk import/export are deferred from v1.

Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. After approval, I’ll prepare the implementation plan—no code has been written yet.

Thanks — this reads clearly and covers the heart of what I asked for: saving links, tagging them, searching and filtering, editing, deleting, and catching duplicates. That's the shape I want.

One thing genuinely matters to me before I sign off, though. The spec says the title and description have to be typed in by hand, and that pulling the page's title automatically is left out of the first version. When I save a bookmark, I really expect to just paste the web address and have the app fill in the page's title (and ideally a short description) for me. Typing a title by hand for every single link is exactly the tedious part I was hoping this app would spare me. For a "save and manage bookmarks" app, automatic title-grabbing on save feels like part of the basic saving experience, not a nice-to-have.

Could you fold that in — when I save a link, the app fetches the page's title automatically, and I can still edit it if I want? I'm fine leaving out the heavier extras you listed (sharing, folders, browser extensions, import/export). I just don't want to be typing titles myself.

Everything else here looks good to me.

content:
Updated the specification to make automatic metadata retrieval part of the core saving experience:

- Pasting a valid URL automatically fills its page title.
- A page-provided short description is filled when available.
- Both fields remain editable.
- If metadata cannot be retrieved, the app creates a readable fallback title so saving is never blocked by manual title entry.
- Private/local network destinations are excluded from metadata retrieval for safety.

The revised [specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md) passes all 16 [quality checks](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md).

Per the `speckit-specify` approval gate, I’ve paused before planning or coding. If you approve this revision, I’ll prepare the implementation plan next.

That's exactly what I was after — I paste a link and the title fills in for me, with a description when it's there, and I can still edit both. The fallback title so saving never gets blocked is a nice touch, and keeping private network addresses out of the fetching for safety is fine by me.

This covers what I wanted. I approve the specification — go ahead and prepare the implementation plan.

The implementation plan is ready for approval.

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md)
- [Technical research](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/research.md)

Key decisions include a single React Router application, SQLite persistence, database-backed authentication, strict per-user isolation, and a server-side metadata fetcher protected against private-network access, DNS rebinding, unsafe redirects, oversized responses, and timeouts. The OpenAPI contract passes validation without warnings.

The specification is now marked approved. Per the `speckit-plan` gate, no application code has been written. Please approve the plan or request revisions; after approval, I’ll generate the dependency-ordered implementation tasks.

This all lines up with what we agreed on — I can save links with the title filled in for me, keep them organized with tags, search and filter, edit, and delete, and my library stays private to me. content:
The implementation task breakdown is ready: [tasks.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/tasks.md).

It contains 75 sequential tasks:

- Setup and shared foundation: 17
- US1 — Save and revisit: 22
- US2 — Browse and organize: 9
- US3 — Search and filter: 8
- US4 — Edit and delete: 9
- Final hardening and delivery: 10

There are 38 parallelizable tasks. Every task follows the required checklist format, has a sequential ID, identifies its story where applicable, and names exact file paths.

The suggested MVP is US1: sign in, paste a URL, retrieve or generate its title, edit the metadata, save and reopen it, handle failures gracefully, and catch duplicates. Each subsequent story has its own independent acceptance checkpoint.

Per the `speckit-tasks` gate, I’ve paused before implementation. Approve this breakdown and I’ll begin executing it.

The task breakdown maps onto everything we agreed: saving with the title filled in, organizing with tags, searching and filtering, and editing and deleting. The MVP starting with saving and reopening a link makes sense to me — that's the heart of it.

Approved — please go ahead and start building.
